historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, Menakā (Sanskrit: मेनका, IAST: Menakā) is the name of a lovely woman, considered the personification of the constellation Pleiades, or the Seven Sisters. She is also known as the wife of the god Garuda, and the mother of Jambavan, the king of the bears. This name is mentioned in various Hindu epics, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas, which were composed between 400 BCE and 400 CE.

Meena (Sanskrit: मीना) is also a common Hindu given name. It is derived from the word ‘mīnā’, which means ‘intense, passionate, or beautiful’. This name is associated with the goddess Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, who is considered the deity of Madurai, in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The name Meena has been in use since at least the 13th century, and is still popular in India today.
